title: Reduzir duplicação de candidatos GitHub por sistema e libc
description: Manifesto pessoal: br exige quatro candidatos github-mac/github-linux/github-musl/github-windows, compartilhando repo/checksum/scope; omp exige três (glibc/musl/darwin), wt exige github-linux/github-mac. Embora {os_any}/{arch_any}/{version} resolvam sinônimos, asset aceita uma única string por candidato, e when atua sobre o candidato inteiro; diferenças só no nome/extensão/entrypoint do asset forçam duplicação de repo e campos comuns. O problema real é seleção de ARTEFATO dentro do mesmo método, não falta de mais métodos. Avaliar extensão mínima e compatível ao schema v1 para variantes de asset condicionadas por os/arch/libc, com overrides estritamente necessários (por exemplo, entrypoints para br.exe) e sem introduzir templates arbitrários, herança genérica ou fallback heurístico. Comparar redução de linhas e comportamento efetivo usando manifests br, omp e wt como fixtures. Preservar prioridade AUR worktrunk-bin sobre native pacman no Arch.
acceptance_criteria: Um método GitHub declara campos comuns + distributions (uma por os/arch/libc, com when obrigatório); especialização pura e determinística antes do plano produz UM candidato efetivo por método, sem criar candidatos extras; zero ou uma distribuição elegível (0 = método inelegível, próximo método; >1 = erro de ambiguidade antes de consultar GitHub); asset literal ou regex explícita com correspondência única; mantém schema_version 1, lock/estado fail-closed para identidades incompatíveis, e inspect why; testes nas fixtures reais br, omp e wt sem mascarar prioridade worktrunk-bin/AUR.
notes:
Auditoria PR #148, HEAD 60963bf: merge bloqueado, PR convertida para Draft em 2026-10-12. Achados pendentes de reproducao/correcao ou descarte fundamentado: dep-1n0.14 (recuperacao de substituicao com distribution efetiva), dep-1n0.15 (GPG nao-terminal apos refetch). Ambos sao issues filhos abertos com label merge-blocker. Nao marcar a PR ready nem fazer merge ate encerrar os dois com testes/evidencia e completar validacao de CI restante.

P1 recovery/GPG regressions are fixed in 6d23b68 and 910f095.

title: PR #148: falha de assinatura GPG apos refetch deve ser terminal
description: Achado da auditoria da PR #148 no commit 60963bf (fluxo inspecionado; reproducao pendente). Em internal/httpdownload/adapter.go verifyDownloadedArtifact converte integrity.ErrSignatureVerification em exec.IntegrityError na primeira verificacao. Se um arquivo vindo do cache falhar checksum e for baixado novamente, o erro da segunda verifyChecksum retorna apenas fmt.Errorf com %w, sem converter a falha GPG. internal/exec/terminal.go nao trata integrity.ErrSignatureVerification isolado como terminal. Hipotese: a segunda verificacao GPG pode falhar e permitir fallback para outro metodo, violando docs/specs/github-distributions.md. Testar com cache corrompido, novo download e sidecar com assinatura invalida; preservar comportamento terminal de mismatch puro.

title: .deb release artifacts have no install lifecycle (dpkg-backed handling missing)
description:
Concrete case hit while packaging git-delta (dandavison/delta) for personal dotfiles: the release publishes amd64/arm64/armhf/i386 .debs plus musl variants, but depengine rejects all HTTP/GitHub .deb lifecycles before download (`rejectUntrackedDebLifecycle`) because package identity is not persisted for observation/removal.

Impact: on Debian/Ubuntu the only depengine route is the apt repo package, which lags badly (repology: ubuntu_24_04 git-delta 0.16.5 vs upstream 0.20.1; debian_13 0.18.2). Users who want the current release .deb cannot express it; the wiki-recommended `dpkg -i file.deb` path has no depengine equivalent.

Possible direction (maintainer decides): a dpkg-backed lifecycle that persists exact package name/arch/version identity at install (dpkg-deb -f) and observes/removes via dpkg-query/dpkg, analogous to how msi tracks product_name/publisher or macpkg tracks package_id. Until then the .deb rejection stands, but it should be tracked as a capability gap rather than only a guardrail.

title: Define a retirement gate for depengine.lock v1 compatibility
description: Mirror of GitHub #143 (open, 2026-10-06). notes: 2026-10-12 implementation evidence: compatibility.md, support-boundary.md, roadmap.md, specs/format-v1-freeze.md, and ADR-001 now distinguish writer/preservation retirement from v1 reader/application retirement. Freeze review alone does not drop v1; reader removal requires explicit compatibility policy for a designated incompatible release and its documented deprecation window to end. Profiled writer/preservation ends once each such update can write a complete v2 projection or fails requiring whole-schema update. Reads/frozen validation/install/status do not silently migrate; format-only migration must be representation-only; whole-schema update is explicit resolution. title: asdf/mise adapter cannot express backend specs (mise use -g github:owner/repo)
description:
Hit packaging oh-my-pi, published in the mise backend form `mise use -g github:can1357/oh-my-pi`.

The depengine asdf adapter only speaks plugin names (`mise install nodejs@20.1.0`, `mise use -g nodejs@20.1.0` — internal/ecosystem/asdf_v2_test.go:69): there is no field for the backend prefix (`github:`, `cargo:`, `npm:`, `go:`, `pipx:`, `aqua:`, ...), so backend-pinned tools cannot be declared at all. mise resolves backends explicitly while asdf uses plugins/shorthands, and the two are not interchangeable here.

Possible directions (maintainer decides): a `backend`/`prefix` field on the asdf method (validated against a known set, defaulting to the current plugin behavior), or document backend specs as unsupported. Note the adapter already detects either binary (asdf or mise); the gap is purely the spec grammar.
notes: Implemented an explicit `backend` field for mise backends aqua/cargo/github/go/npm/pipx; it is validated as an enum and carried as a backend-qualified resolved package through plan/install/observe/check/remove. Without the field, existing asdf/mise plugin behavior is unchanged. Focused Runner lifecycle test covers `github:can1357/oh-my-pi@1.2.3` with install, global use, version observation/check, and uninstall; validation test rejects unknown backend. `go test ./internal/ecosystem ./internal/validate ./internal/methodkind -count=1` passed. Local mise binary unavailable (`mise --version` -> command not found), so a real executable smoke could not be run.
close_reason: Fixed plan identity to retain raw package plus backend source; full Executor CLI smoke verified install/status/remove using a checksum-verified mise binary and temporary npm registry. Focused Go tests pass.

title: Keep locked Homebrew tap revision effective during install
description:
Keep a resolved non-empty brew-tap source revision effective during Homebrew package installation by setting HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 only for that install child process. Preserve exact source preflight and fail-closed per-child environment execution.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Native macOS brew and explicit brew-manager InstallResolved paths detect a resolved brew-tap source iff its resolved revision is non-empty.
2. Preserve brew install <resolved package> argv and post-install verification; only the relevant install gets HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1. No parent environment mutation; no override for unpinned sources, missing source, or non-Brew managers.
3. Keep source-origin/local-HEAD preflight unchanged; preserve run.RunWithEnv fail-closed behavior if Runner lacks EnvironmentRunner.
4. Permanent behavior tests cover both entrypoints and pinned/unpinned/no-source/non-Brew cases, asserting env presence/absence, unchanged argv, and postcondition using an env-recording Runner (FakeRunner discards env).
5. Narrowly update docs/support-boundary.md to state auto-update is disabled for locked-revision Brew installs without claiming tap content/dependencies/artifacts or concurrent external brew update are pinned; update CHANGELOG. Leave broad docs/roadmap.md umbrella unchecked.
6. Smoke changed adapter path with a runner-recording test/script, run focused source/run/native tests and appropriate full gates. Do not claim an actual Homebrew host install if unavailable. No generic retry, validation, telemetry, or unrelated Homebrew lifecycle work.

title: Decidir e implementar portão de código arbitrário sobre candidatos inelegíveis
description:
## Contexto

Relatório preliminar `.dev/report-scalability-planning.md` (base master @ 4207205, confirmado no HEAD atual): o portão de código arbitrário `hasDangerousMethod` (`internal/exec/hooks.go:18`) itera todos os candidatos selecionados e monta/valida o plano completo de cada um (`candidatePlanIntent` → `BuildValidatedCandidateIntent` → `plan.Validate`), inclusive os que o `when` excluiria. Perfil com 480 candidatos: `hasDangerousMethod` 63% da CPU de planejamento. Experimento: desligar o portão reduz ~37–46 µs para ~11–14 µs por candidato (~70% do custo em schemas enumerados).

Reconfirmado no HEAD: o laço de `hasDangerousMethod` (`hooks.go:18-25`) continua sem chamar `When.Match`; `SelectMethods` (`internal/config/method_order.go:16`) só ordena.

Hoje o comportamento é fail-closed: uma ferramenta com candidato perigoso que o `when` exclui é bloqueada sem `--allow-arbitrary-code`.

## Escopo

Decisão de segurança (mantenedor) + implementação:

- (a) manter e aceitar o custo;
- (b) pular candidatos que o `when` exclui dentro do laço de `hasDangerousMethod` (não altera a lista de candidatos nem a identidade do lock);
- (c) memoizar por candidato.

Restrição dura: quando os fatos do host são desconhecidos/incompletos, o comportamento deve continuar fail-closed (não pular candidacy com base em `when` não avaliável).

Se (b) for aprovada: implementar com testes (candidato perigoso excluído por `when` não bloqueia; candidato perigoso elegível continua bloqueando), rerodar o benchmark de planejamento para confirmar a queda, e commitar `internal/exec/planning_bench_test.go` em master como régua de regressão.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decisão registrada refletindo o estado atual: (d) no bead irmão dep-gate-lean-operations-bit-7j4, (a) no ínterim, (b) adiada com guarda de inelegibilidade conclusiva, (c) rejeitada — com a semântica fail-closed para fatos de host desconhecidos/incompletos explicitada.
- Gatilhos de reativação de (b) operacionalizados: (i) benchmark pós-(d) (régua do bead irmão) ainda dominante na forma enumerada; (ii) NÃO mensurável hoje — não há corpus; (b) revive por (i)+(iii); quando o catálogo existir, medir prevalência restrita a superfícies method-level (hooks de ferramenta tripam o gate independentemente de when — métrica que não discriminar mede errado); (iii) forma E/N revelada pelo spike dep-spike-catalog-host-specialization-pyx.
- Condição de morte: se a direção de catálogo for abandonada, (b) fecha como wontfix em vez de apodrecer aberta.
- Questão aberta registrada: conclusividade de campos bool (IsWSL/IsContainer/IsAndroid) na guarda futura de (b) — bools sem tri-state tornam "desconhecido" indistinguível de "não"; precisa de resposta antes de implementar a guarda.
- Se (b) for um dia implementada: candidato perigoso excluído por when NÃO bloqueia a ferramenta; candidato perigoso elegível continua bloqueando; fatos nil/unknown/inconclusivos NUNCA pulam; helper único de elegibilidade compartilhado com attempt/batch/explain/lock_resolution; property test executado ⊆ contado; testes cobrindo ambos os casos.
- Nenhuma mudança na lista de candidatos nem na identidade de lock/MethodsHash.
close_reason: Decisão registrada e item acionável (d) entregue em 462c816, com benchmark pós-(d) confirmando gatilho (i); (b) permanece adiada por falta de corpus/catálogo e de guarda tri-estado conclusiva; (c) rejeitada; (a) mantida no ínterim. title: curl|bash and irm|iex installer scripts have no method equivalent
description:
Hit packaging oh-my-pi (and earlier beads_rust): both upstreams document `curl -fsSL <url> | sh` / `irm <url> | iex` as primary install routes, and depengine cannot express them.

- The http/github adapters download artifacts and never execute installer scripts (internal/httpdownload/adapter.go:423 materializes the download as a file). Pointing `url` at an install.sh would install the script text as the tool binary.
- The only adjacent primitive is hooks (pre_install/post_install run blocks), which are wrong for this: they run on every install/upgrade transition, are not idempotent, cannot observe or remove what the script installed, and still need --allow-arbitrary-code.
- So installer-script upstreams must be re-expressed per-artifact (github raw binaries + checksum_url, aur, nix flake, brew tap...), which duplicates the routing logic the script already encodes (glibc/musl selection, checksum verification, skills/PATH side effects).

Possible directions (maintainer decides): an explicit `script` method kind with declared interpreter, pinned checksum of the script itself, owned-path declarations for check/remove, and no rc-file mutation; or keep scripts out of scope and document the re-expression pattern (what was done for br/omp) in schema-reference so authors stop trying `url = ...install.sh`.
notes:

title: Make dpkg native observation authoritative
description: Root cause: dpkg-backed native observation currently treats every nonzero dpkg -s result as package absence, while dpkg can report config-files residuals as success and database/query failures as nonzero. Implement an authoritative structured dpkg-query observation protocol for Debian apt and Termux; identify installed dpkg as the database-health sentinel using dpkg-query defaults (no hardcoded status path or environment mutation). Match exact package identity including architecture; fail unknown on missing sentinel, ambiguous multiarch, malformed states/output, Err, WaitErr, or unsupported status. Interpret dpkg Status as desired/error/actual. Require valid tokens and error=ok; actual=installed is Present regardless of desired state (including install, hold, deinstall, or purge), while actual=config-files or not-installed is Absent. Malformed tokens and all other actual/error states are Unknown/Broken. Migrate every affected v2 consumer; preserve other native providers intentionally.
acceptance_criteria:
- Real container probes cover installed, genuinely absent, config-files residual, malformed/missing DB, and multiarch exact identity.
- Native default, explicit apt, and Termux observations are authoritative; query ambiguity/failure is Unknown/Broken, never Absent.
- Check/status/idempotency/postinstall/batch/remove/undo/recovery paths consume this result without unsafe state deletion or mutation; consumer-visible regressions remain covered.
- Provider-specific conformance distinguishes recognized dpkg absence from operational failure; other managers remain unchanged/documented.
- Docs explain invariant, rationale, alternatives, failure semantics, state/lock interaction, and per-provider follow-up gate; no lock version is inferred from observation.
notes:
Protocol: one structured target+dpkg sentinel query; missing/damaged sentinel or ambiguous/malformed/error states remain Unknown. dpkg Status is desired/error/actual: error=ok plus actual=installed is Present regardless desired state (including hold/deinstall/purge); error=ok plus not-installed/config-files is Absent; other states Unknown. Unqualified single multiarch row can prove presence while preserving requested identity; multiple rows are Unknown.
Protocol refinement: query the exact requested package and dpkg sentinel independently (deduplicate when target=dpkg). Real Debian CLI proved a combined query with a missing target returns exit 1 and no rows, including no sentinel, so it cannot validate absence. Two bounded structured dpkg-query calls avoid full inventory copying/caching. Present and residual target records still require a healthy sentinel; only clean target exit 1 with empty stdout plus healthy sentinel proves absent. Status desired/error/actual accepts held/deinstall/purge actual-installed when error=ok; config-files/not-installed absent; incomplete/malformed unknown.

`.dev/report-scalability-planning.md` item 4 do veredito: catálogo por lookup de nome (manifest aponta para catálogos; filtro por nome vira consulta). Risco central registrado ali: **especializar o catálogo por host reduz a lista de candidatos e pode quebrar identidade de candidato** — lock v1 usa chaves `<tool>/<method>/<index>`, `MethodsHash` considera a sequência de `Kind`/`Label`, e a validação não pode depender só do host atual.

O manifest hoje paga o catálogo inteiro: `ParseManifest` lê o arquivo completo e depois `FilterManifestTools` descarta por nome (`internal/config/manifest.go:76-82`, `internal/app/helpers.go:139-143`). Semântica já é pull-by-name; mecanismo é eager.

## Escopo (spike isolado, sem mudar produção)

Seguir o processo de `dep-1n0.1` (spike A×C): baseline em goldens + critérios *no-go* declarados antes de medir.

Pergunta central: um catálogo especializado por host mantém estáveis (1) índices de candidato, (2) pins do lock v1, (3) `MethodsHash`? Se não mantiver, o desenho muda (ex.: especializar só materialização, nunca ordem/identidade).

Critérios no-go mínimos propostos (confirmar antes de executar):
- Qualquer divergência de `MethodsHash` entre catálogo geral e especializado no mesmo host é no-go para especialização por host.
- Qualquer shift de índice `<tool>/<method>/<index>` para o mesmo par schema+host é no-go.
- Validação que só passa no host que gerou o catálogo é no-go (contrato exige validar hosts declarados).

Pré-requisito de sequência: o mantenedor espera o conflito de identidade de candidato do item 8.1 de dep-1n0 resolvido antes de fundir desenho; spike pode rodar em paralelo, mas conclusão/agregação espera essa decisão.
acceptance_criteria:
- Baseline em goldens antes de prototipar; critérios no-go declarados na issue antes de rodar.
- Resposta explícita (sim/não + evidência) para: índices de candidato estáveis? pins v1 estáveis? MethodsHash estável?
- Nenhum arquivo de produção alterado; relatório em .dev/ e issue atualizada.
- Conclusão/agregação do desenho espera a resolução do conflito de identidade de candidato do item 8.1 de dep-1n0.
notes: Correção de referência (2026-10-17, council #2): o pré-requisito de sequência citava "o conflito de identidade de candidato do item 8.1 de dep-1n0" como bloqueio, mas dep-1n0 está FECHADA desde 2026-10-12 (fronteira E aprovada no comentário 11 e implementada no PR #148, presente no HEAD 4207205). A referência de bloqueio apodreceu; revalidar se o conflito de identidade ainda é bloqueador real antes de planejar o spike. Achado registrado no council #2 (comentário em dep-gate-arbitrary-code-ineligible-iyn).
close_reason: Spike complete: host-filtered candidate lists break candidate indices, v1 pins, and MethodsHash; host-independent Lookup(name) plus in-candidate specialization preserves them. Reports contain baseline/no-go evidence and cost measurements. Obsolete dep-1n0 8.1 blocker removed; no production changes.

comments.author: khorea
comments.text: Concluded from .dev/reports/report-spike-catalog-identity-2026-10-17.md and report-spike-pyx-catalog-cost-2026-10-18.md. No-go criteria were declared before measurement. Answers: (1) candidate indices stable only for name lookup without host facts; slicing the candidate list per host renumbers them and is a no-go. (2) v1 pins are stable under the same no-host-facts lookup by construction; host-filtered lists change <tool>/<kind>/<index>. (3) MethodsHash is stable for full host-independent recipes and for form E specialization inside a candidate, but not for host-filtered candidate lists. Design conclusion: catalog Lookup(name) must return the complete host-independent recipe; specialize only inside candidates, never by removing/reordering methods. The dep-1n0 item 8.1 prerequisite is obsolete: dep-1n0 closed 2026-10-12 and form E shipped in #148. Remaining work is catalog pinning/layer decisions in ADR-008, not this spike. No production files changed.

title: Broaden shared AdapterV2 and executor conformance coverage
description:
## Objective
Turn the partial P3 roadmap entry “Cover each method contract across validation, identity, dry-run, version, source, scope, environment, lock, lifecycle, idempotency, errors, and secret redaction” into a bounded, executable test task. Expand shared AdapterV2/executor conformance coverage centered on `internal/exectest` and `internal/exec`, adding package-specific fixtures only where needed. Tests only: do not change production code, public APIs, optional capability interfaces, docs, or roadmap.

## Motivation and evidence
The current `internal/exectest.TestAdapterConformance` checks stable nonempty `Kind`, that `Available` does not panic, and that `Observe` returns a recognized `Presence`. A quality audit found lifecycle, identity, dry-run, and related behavior coverage remains provider-specific. The roadmap marks the broader contract coverage partial (`docs/roadmap.md`, P3). Duplicate search found no Beads issue titled/desc-described for conformance, `AdapterV2`, or `exectest`; the ready queue was empty and only `dep-wbg` / `dep-mhp` were blocked.

## Contracts and boundaries
- `methodkind.Contracts` is authoritative for declared fields, effects, and supported capabilities; derive applicable assertions from it.
- Preserve `exec.AdapterV2`, executor/state WAL and ownership semantics, `run.Runner`, and fail-closed handling of unknown/broken observations.
- Do not add production APIs, optional capability interfaces, or assertions for unsupported method capabilities.
- Use deterministic fake-runner isolation. Tests must assert consumer-visible behavior, not method forwarding/wiring, mock echo, or tautologies.
- Keep this a bounded shared conformance suite; retain provider-specific cases when semantics genuinely differ.

## Relevant files
- `internal/exectest/adapter.go` and its tests
- `internal/exec/` executor, AdapterV2, lifecycle/recovery tests
- `internal/methodkind/` contract declarations
- Applicable adapter package tests/fixtures when needed
- `docs/roadmap.md` is context only; do not edit it in this task.

## Dependencies
No Beads dependency. Use existing `methodkind.Contracts`, AdapterV2, executor, and runner contracts as the source of truth. Do not depend on or duplicate blocked `dep-wbg` / `dep-mhp` work.

## Acceptance criteria
- Shared conformance tests exercise consumer-visible resolution/identity and observation behavior according to declared method contracts.
- Where declared capabilities permit, cover install, idempotency, removal, recovery, error handling, dry-run, version/source/scope/environment/lock effects, and secret redaction; explicitly skip or leave provider-specific behaviors where unsupported.
- Lifecycle and ownership assertions cover meaningful state transitions, WAL recovery, and state retention/cleanup without claiming stronger guarantees than the contract.
- Fake-runner tests are deterministic and isolated; failure cases prove unknown/broken results fail closed and do not authorize mutation or state loss.
- Assertions detect incorrect behavior rather than merely confirming forwarding, wiring, mock echo, or their own setup.
- No production code, APIs, optional interfaces, docs, roadmap, or unrelated issue changes.

## Required validation
- `go test -race ./internal/exectest ./internal/exec` plus tests for any touched adapter packages.
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `golangci-lint run`

## Priority
P3 (roadmap P3 verification/conformance gap).

title: Git Observe reports actual installed commit for upgrade reconciliation
description:
## Objective
Correct the Git adapter's owned-checkout observation so reconciliation sees the commit actually installed, not the requested rev/branch/tag selector. This is required for a tracked A→B upgrade: current `Observe` returns `PresenceAbsent` when A differs from desired B, causing `depengine upgrade` to fail instead of replacing the tracked installation.

## Evidence
Actual CLI reproduction on integration behavior used a disposable bare Git repository over loopback dumb HTTP (`git update-server-info`, `depth=0`), no fake adapter/runner. `update` pinned A (`d03d78cda2d2941ffefa2904fb29de2bf2a6bd2a`); install succeeded and reported payload A; repeated install reported Already. The repository branch was advanced to B (`bda6bb37b9e512dad0ebfa0bc3500a4352d0848e`), `update` pinned B, but `upgrade --json --allow-arbitrary-code --force` exited 1: “locked target is absent; run install before upgrade”; payload and ToolState remained A. The extracted checkout had actual HEAD A and only `refs/remotes/origin/main`; `git rev-parse HEAD main` failed because `main` was not a local ref. Current `internal/git/adapter.go:96-110` treats probe failure or target mismatch as absent and reports `Revision: ref`; `internal/app/upgrade.go:246-252` correctly fails closed when reconciliation says install/absent. The root cause is provider observation, not executor upgrade policy.

## Contract boundaries
- In the existing `extract_to` owned-checkout path only, query and report the actual committed `HEAD`; do not report the requested selector as observed identity.
- Keep only `plan.FieldRevision` authoritative. Do not add origin/source projection or change other identity dimensions.
- Accept only full Git object IDs of 40 or 64 hexadecimal characters. Malformed/empty/non-commit HEAD output is broken evidence; Git probe failures must propagate as errors or `PresenceBroken`, never become `PresenceAbsent`.
- Preserve authoritative absence when no owned checkout is present, current fallback strategies, legacy `Check` semantics, resource ownership, and executor/WAL behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- A valid owned checkout at HEAD A with requested/resolved B is observed `PresencePresent`, with known `FieldRevision=A`; shared reconciliation reports `drifted` rather than `absent`.
- Matching A is `satisfied`. 40- and 64-hex commit IDs are accepted; malformed, abbreviated, non-hex, or extra-line HEAD output is broken; a failed probe is surfaced as an error/broken observation and is not absent.
- Exact `depengine upgrade` flow with real Git A→B changes payload and durable ToolState to B without bypassing discovery-time tracked state; subsequent `remove` removes only the owned extraction and releases ToolState/ownership.
- No changes to source/origin projections, generic executor policy, `Check`, or state/WAL ownership semantics.

## Verification
Run focused Git adapter observation/reconciliation tests and a real localhost HTTP Git A→B upgrade/remove CLI smoke using an isolated HOME/XDG/state. Run race suite for touched packages after integration.
acceptance_criteria: A valid owned checkout reports full actual HEAD as known Revision regardless of requested ref; A→B reconciliation is drifted, and real lock-pinned CLI upgrade then remove updates payload/state and releases only owned resources. Non-40/64hex/malformed HEAD or probe failure is broken/error, never absent. No source projection, Check, executor, or WAL policy changes.

title: Fail closed on opaque Git lock-revision verification
description: Separate follow-up risk, not part of the authorized checkout-backed Git observation fix. Code evidence at base 8011b8bb3608ef5f55681c56f8310f54e7a48266: internal/app/upgrade.go:208-257 resolves a v2 candidate, calls TransitionForVerification, then skips it unless the transition is Upgrade. A presence-only Git observation with no projected desired revision can reconcile Satisfied and therefore be silently omitted from the upgrade set, even when the lock resolves an explicit new revision. Git methodkind currently treats url/branch/tag/rev as Resolve|Execute; binary and managed_paths establish existence, not source revision. This is a bounded detection/completeness risk for opaque Git installations, distinct from a checkout whose .git directory permits actual HEAD observation. Existing presence-only checks are not a promise of full revision verification; document that limitation truthfully while addressing explicit lock upgrades.

title: Whole-schema update cannot migrate native-heavy schemas to v2 lock
description:
Whole-schema `depengine update` (no --profile) over a readable v1 lock always takes the v2 projection path (`canPersistProjection`, internal/app/universal_lock.go:190) and fails closed when any non-virtual tool lacks an immutable identity (`internal/plan/lock.go:706`).

Native adapters never expose one: `NativeAdapter.ResolvePlan` and `NativeByManagerAdapter.ResolvePlan` (internal/exec/native_adapter.go:130,418) return the intent clone with package identity only — no version, revision, digest, or artifacts. Non-winget `Observe` is exit-code-only by design.

Minimal repro on cachyos/arch x86_64, commit a88dfe6 (fresh `go install`):
schema_version = 1, `[tools] simple = ["zsh"]`, empty v1 lock →
`universal lock: lock document: zsh/native: immutable lock identity unavailable: manager did not expose a stable resolved identity`

Same failure on a real 71-tool native-heavy schema (personal dotfiles): first unresolvable candidates (dead p7zip, phantom serpantinum/rshred/glide-bin packages — fixed in dotfiles), then hard stop at `7zip/native` (installed, 26.04-1.1).

Impact: any schema containing a plain native tool can never whole-schema `update`; the lock is stuck on v1 and `make setup`-style flows that run `depengine update` fail deterministically. The support-boundary "all-or-nothing" rule assumes every manager can expose a stable identity, which native managers currently cannot.

Possible directions (maintainer decides): resolve native identity from installed (`pacman -Q`) or repo (`pacman -Si`) version for the projection; or keep whole-schema update on the legacy v1 path when v2 coverage is unprovable instead of failing.
notes:
2026-10-12 implementation paused for explicit product direction: native ResolvePlan currently supplies package identity only; non-winget observation is presence-only, and v2 projection correctly fails closed without immutable version/revision/digest/artifact identity. Recommended retain v2 all-or-nothing and implement native v2 locking only per manager when exact version resolution and exact-version replay are both supported/tested. Do not preserve v1 as an implicit whole-schema update success; that path cannot claim native package versions are pinned. Main notified with proposal; no behavior/doc change made.
2026-10-12 maintainer decision: keep v2 projection all-or-nothing and fail-closed; no partial v2 and no implicit v1 success/fallback. This remains an architectural limitation, not a resolved behavior fix. Evidence: NativeAdapter.ResolvePlan/NativeByManagerAdapter.ResolvePlan return the plan with package identity only; non-winget Observe reports package presence only. A simple native package name therefore does not encode an immutable version. The projection correctly rejects missing version/revision/digest/checksum/artifact identity. Resolution condition: implement and test manager-specific concrete-version resolution plus exact-version install/replay through lifecycle, for each manager before advertising native v2 lockability. No extra flag or partial projection. Updated compatibility.md v2 migration condition, support-boundary native limitation, README, roadmap, and generated update docs; update error now adds the tool/method error plus a hint that native package names are not version pins and no partial v2 was written. Issue remains blocked/open for the architectural implementation; do not close as fixed.

Resolution requires manager-specific concrete version/revision/digest identity plus matching exact-version install/replay and tests for each manager; not currently implemented. Do not close this issue until that capability exists. Updated compatibility/support-boundary/README/roadmap and depengine update diagnostics to say whole-schema update may fail, leaves v1 unchanged, and writes no partial projection; native package name/presence is not a pin.
